subject: DataLink RFI — jurisdictional storage, TTLs, and erasure timelines
messages:
From: Samira Qureshi <security@dataportal.io>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Alice Chan <alice.chan@dataportal.io>, legal@dataportal.io
Date: Sun, 7 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: RFI — Data residency + TTL questions for Hosted API

Hi Irene,

Thanks for taking this. As part of our procurement review for the integration with Redwood's Hosted API, our security team has a short set of questions focused on where data lives, how long it is retained, and how erasure is handled. We need written answers for our vendor security pack. Could you confirm the following for our EU tenant (DataLink EU):

1) Where customer payloads are stored (region/zone) immediately after ingestion and for persisted artifacts (logs, traces, embeddings).
2) Default time-to-live (TTL) for non-persistent request data, persisted embeddings, and any queued/batch work.
3) Erasure workflow: once a deletion request is issued (API or support ticket), how quickly is data removed from primary storage, caches, and backups?
4) Logical vs physical deletion — do you provide attestations for cryptographic key destruction or physical media wipe for on-prem/dedicated contracts?
5) Any exceptions where data might be replicated outside EU for operational reasons (diagnostics, failover) and the controls in place.

We'd like the response in bullet form and a short diagram if possible. If you can include attachments or a matrix we can include directly in our evidence pack that would be ideal.

Best,
Samira
Security Analyst — DataPortal

---

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Samira Qureshi <security@dataportal.io>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 7 Jul 2028 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: RFI — Data residency + TTL questions for Hosted API

Hi Samira —

Thanks for the clear list. Below are concise answers you can drop into your pack; I attached a dataflow diagram and a retention matrix for DataLink EU (see attachments). If you need a signed attestation, we can route that through our security attestations process — note that takes 2–3 business days once requested.

1) Storage locations
- Ingestion: transient buffers in the EU region closest to the tenant (primarily eu-west-1 and eu-central-1 depending on routing).
- Persisted artifacts: customer-linked metadata, embeddings, and audit logs are stored in EU-backed storage (S3 equivalent in eu region).
- Access logs and telemetry: retained in EU for default tenants; telemetry used for platform health may be copied to a secured EU logging cluster and only forwarded to non-EU endpoints with explicit contractual exceptions.

2) Default TTLs (DataLink tenant defaults)
- Non-persistent request data (streaming generation context, prefix cache): ephemeral by default and evicted within 24 hours unless explicitly cached by your application (configurable).
- Persisted embeddings: default TTL 365 days; configurable per-tenant down to 0 days (ephemeral).
- Queued/batch artifacts: kept for up to 7 days by default; shorter retention possible via queue policy.

3) Erasure workflow and timelines
- API-initiated deletion: primary storage deletion operations are scheduled immediately. Typical primary-store removal: within 4 hours.
- Cache/KV eviction: within 6–8 hours for mostly-in-memory caches; strong invalidation is issued at delete time.
- Backups/snapshots: application-level backups are on a rolling cadence (daily snapshots). Deletion from backups: we mark records for removal and purge in the next snapshot cycle; full purge from backup rotation completes within 30 days (we provide a purge confirmation when completed).
- Audit trail: deletion actions are logged to an immutable audit stream (customer-visible).

4) Logical vs physical deletion / attestations
- Hosted API: we perform logical deletion (data rendered inaccessible and removed from indexes) and schedule physical purge per backup rotation described above. For customers requiring stronger proof, we offer an attestation package for deletion events (signed by our security team).
- Dedicated/Private deployments: for on-prem or dedicated capacity customers, we support customer-side KMS with key destruction workflows; physical media wipe options are available for on-prem engagements and can be contractually specified.

5) Replication exceptions and controls
- Default behavior: no cross-region replication outside the tenant's region set (EU) for customer payloads.
- Operational exceptions: in rare failover scenarios, we may route to an adjacent EU region; we do not replicate to non-EU regions without contractual consent.
- Diagnostics: anonymized diagnostic snippets may be routed to support clusters; full payloads are never routed outside EU without explicit legal/contractual approval.
- Controls: contractual addendum, IP allow-listing, and audit logging for any cross-region actions.

Attachments included: Dataflow-Diagram.pdf (high-level flow), Retention-Matrix-DataLink.csv (TTL table), HostedAPI-Residency-Annex.pdf (supporting policy excerpts).

If any of these timings are blockers for procurement, flag which line items you need tightened and I will loop in our platform engineering team.

Regards,
Irene Choi
Security & Compliance — Redwood Inference

---

From: Samira Qureshi <security@dataportal.io>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Alice Chan <alice.chan@dataportal.io>
Date: Mon, 8 Jul 2028 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: RFI — Data residency + TTL questions for Hosted API

Thanks Irene — this is very helpful. Two quick clarifications from our side: 

A) Backups: when you say "purge from backup rotation completes within 30 days" — is that an SLA-backed commitment for Hosted API customers, or an operational target? We need to understand if DataLink can require a contractual commitment.

B) Key destruction: for Dedicated/Private you mention KMS with key destruction workflows — can you share a short note on whether key destruction is irreversible (i.e., would that make data unrecoverable) and whether you will provide a signed key-destruction certificate?

Also, can you confirm whether any support access for debugging requires cross-region escalation and what controls exist for those sessions (e.g., session recordings, just-in-time privileges)?

Appreciate the quick follow-up.
Samira

Subject: Re: RFI — Data residency + TTL questions for Hosted API

Samira — quick follow-up and confirmations: 

A) Backups SLA vs target
- For standard Hosted API customers the 30-day backup purge is an operational target and part of our retention policy; it is not included in the standard Hosted SLA.
- For customers with contractual requirements (e.g., enterprise procurement), we can include a contractual backup purge commitment in the Dedicated or Enterprise addendum; we have templates that define a shorter backup purge window and associated penalties.

B) KMS key destruction
- For Dedicated/Private deployments using customer-managed keys (CMK), key destruction is irreversible: once the KMS key material is destroyed, ciphertext cannot be decrypted and data is effectively unrecoverable.
- We provide a signed key-destruction certificate for on-prem and dedicated engagements upon request; standard Hosted tenants can request an attestation package for deletion events but do not receive a KMS key-destruction certificate unless using a dedicated KMS integration.

C) Support access controls
- Cross-region escalation: support engineers require explicit justification and are granted minimal, time-limited access via JIT (just-in-time) privileged sessions.
- Session controls: all sessions are recorded and archived in the EU logging cluster for tenant requests; privileged actions require two-person approval in sensitive cases.
- Customer notification: we notify customers for support sessions that access customer content unless emergency conditions apply; all access is logged and available via the console audit view.

Next steps: I have uploaded the retention matrix and the diagram to the shared drive link below and can generate a signed deletion attestation or enterprise addendum if DataLink wants contractual language. If you want the backup purge window shortened to 14 days in contract, mark that in your RFI and I will route to legal/ops for a proposal.

Link: https://drive.redwood.com/shared/DR-4512/Retention-Matrix-DataLink.csv

Regards,
Irene Choi
Security & Compliance — Redwood Inference
